checks.message: runScriptLocal retries an impossible launch until the fixture interrupts it.
A successfully launched but dead child leaves its caller waiting for a port reply.
A fresh remote stockmaster receives no reserve/config; an empty local reserve reads as zero.
Cracker inventory omits BruteSSH-only ownership and reports FTP-only as BruteSSH.
$1m cash / $900k reserve still buys nine $110k servers, leaving $10k.
Intel readiness is never refreshed in the loop; the finish gate remains tied to startup intent.
Sleeve purchaser makes zero attempts after live cash rises above price; player was read once.
Both reset-time hash liquidation and home-RAM upgrade targets are missing files.
BN6/SF6-only access is rejected by both Bladeburner launch and entry gates.
alwaysRun=true suppresses the periodic launch even when the script is absent.
A one-augmentation batch calls no purchase API but reports the entire $100 budget as spent.
An API failure is truthy to the ascend upgrade loop; strict result validation is required.
Hash server upgrades receive an object unless --spend-on-server supplies a hostname.
The failure file suppresses notices but does not prevent a second attempt on the same contract.
Post-batch leftover threads become NaN; the target-switch call also lacks await/hostname.
Batch calculator fixture adds 0.18 security and budgets 0.05 weakening at BN1/one core.
maxRun selects 512 GB on an unrooted host and ignores the rooted 128/64 GB hosts.
Stasis branch requests 22 threads / 540.1 GB from 128 GB free.
